_comment: Example hooks file for PeerParty (docs/usage.md, 'A game's own libcurl').
One file per module, named after it: this one is for MyGame-Win64-Shipping.exe. Put it in
%LOCALAPPDATA%\peerparty\patterns\ (or the folder PEERPARTY_PATTERNS_DIR names). A DLL's
file works the same way (SomeLibrary.dll.json).
Each entry of 'versions' is for one build of the module: 'sha256' (of the module's file)
and/or 'file_version' (its version resource, a.b.c.d) say which; an entry with neither is
for any build. The log prints a module's version and SHA-256 when no entry is for it.
Of the entries that match, one with a sha256 wins, then one with a file_version, then one
with neither.
Patterns: hex bytes, '??' for a byte that changes (call and jump offsets, addresses).
The first pattern that matches exactly one place is used. curl_easy_setopt_patterns and
curl_easy_cleanup_patterns are both needed; curl_easy_reset_patterns only if the game calls
curl_easy_reset. A pattern needs at least 6 fixed bytes, at most 256 bytes in all, and
starts at the function's first byte.
curl_easy_setopt_patterns is curl_easy_setopt itself, the function with the '...': in x64
it starts by storing rdx, r8 and r9 (89 54 24 10 4C 89 44 24 18 4C 89 4C 24 20) and
returns 43 for a NULL handle. Not Curl_vsetopt, the one it calls with a va_list (it
keeps r8 as that va_list and goes straight into a switch on the option): hooked as
curl_easy_setopt, it would be handed the wrong arguments.
Keys that start with '_' are notes and are ignored.

versions._build: One exact build, by its SHA-256 (made up here).
Any build with this file version.
Any other build: looser patterns, tried last.
